name: Gangrel Clan Society and Powers (Clanbook: Gangrel, Ch. 2)

text.content:
In the years leading into the modern nights, the Gangrel justicar Xaviar abruptly and unilaterally withdrew Clan Gangrel from the Camarilla, delivering a single sentence to the sect's Inner Circle and never publicly explaining himself further. No clan had ever left the Camarilla before, and no precedent exists for the sect to compel a clan's return. The Inner Circle has not called a conclave to address the departure, and the remaining justicars have made no move to appoint a new Gangrel justicar to restore representation, despite pressure from Ventrue and Toreador elders who fear the precedent an unaddressed clan secession sets. Other elders, chiefly among the Tremere and Toreador, argue the reverse: that the clan's departure is simply and rightly the sect's loss, and some have called for remaining Gangrel to be stripped of office and evicted from the Camarilla outright.

The rank and file of Clan Gangrel largely followed Xaviar's lead out of the sect, though few of them have ever met him and the clan has no unifying leadership structure that could have ordered a mass withdrawal. Every Gangrel who has not lost themselves to the Beast can offer a garbled version of the rumored cause: that Xaviar personally witnessed some being of terrible, unconfirmed power — possibly a waking Antediluvian, possibly something from the Book of Nod — and concluded that the Camarilla's Inner Circle has been lying about what it knows. Asked directly, most Gangrel offer only sullen silence or one of several deliberately absurd stock phrases that have become an inside joke traded among clan members in place of a real answer. At least one Camarilla justicar has reportedly moved (without yet gathering the support to act) to place Xaviar on the Red List for spreading this claim as heresy.

Storyteller/Player use: Treat "the Gangrel left the Camarilla" as a concrete, datable in-setting event and political fact, not mere flavor — it should govern how Camarilla NPCs and Traits (Status, Influence, city Domain access) treat any Gangrel character. A Gangrel PC who remains nominally Camarilla is swimming against clan opinion and sect suspicion simultaneously; see "Gangrel Who Remain Camarilla" and "Gangrel Autarkis" below for the two most common outcomes Storytellers can hand to such characters.

Not every Gangrel left with Xaviar. Karsh, the Warlord, is the most prominent Gangrel to remain a Camarilla member in good standing, and a number of Gangrel archons still serve the justicars. Rank-and-file Gangrel in Camarilla-held cities also remain for their own reasons — existing contacts, outstanding promises of service, or territorial interests — and clanmates generally respect service-based reasons for staying more than territorial ones.

Mechanically and socially, Camarilla Gangrel now pay a steep price for their loyalty. Other Kindred openly suspect them of having "gone over to the Sabbat," Camarilla princes are parceling out formerly Gangrel-held domain and hunting grounds to better-connected Kindred, and along contested fronts (the North American East Coast is called out by name) Gangrel are as likely to be destroyed on sight as questioned. A Storyteller running a Camarilla-affiliated Gangrel character should treat this as an active, ongoing Status/Influence penalty and source of city-level suspicion, not merely as color: any domain or Boon-based Trait test involving a Camarilla NPC's treatment of a Gangrel character should default to a harsher difficulty or an explicit precondition (proof of continued loyalty, a favor called in, etc.) unless the Storyteller rules otherwise for that chronicle.

The Camarilla calls unaligned Gangrel "Autarkis"; the Sabbat calls them "fencesitters"; to themselves, they are simply Gangrel. Independents have always been the clan's numerical heart, maintaining cordial relations across the Camarilla/Sabbat divide, with the anarchs, and even occasionally with the Inconnu. Since Xaviar's departure, a new wave of "orphans of the Camarilla" — vampires with only a decade or three of Camarilla existence, who left the sect purely out of respect for Xaviar's example — now swells the Autarkis' ranks, often unprepared for unlife without the Masquerade's institutional safety net.

Gangrel independents have no overarching organization by design, but they do self-organize on a smaller scale: by geography (respecting either mortal political boundaries, such as a US state, or a terrain feature, such as a river valley), or around the charisma and reputation of an individual mentor or sire. Geographically-linked Gangrel hold seasonal moots and treat invitations from within their territory as effectively compulsory — repeated no-shows draw a visit from concerned (and potentially violent) neighbors. Politically-inclined elders and sires who remember historical raiding cultures have begun reviving older tribal identities — jarls accepting oaths of loyalty in exchange for loot and feasting, styled after Vikings, Huns, Goths, Mongols, Gauls, Aztecs, and Sioux war-band structures — forming named "ethnic" broods across the Americas and Europe that both Camarilla princes and Sabbat bishops watch warily.

Two independent Gangrel prides claim to have successfully tracked Xaviar down to question him directly; they do not get along especially well with each other, but continue to cooperate.

Clan Gangrel has had a presence in the Sabbat since its founding; Gangrel sires rarely favor tradition-bound childer, and willful progeny often sided with the anarchs during the sect wars. Jalan-Aajav, Seraph of the Black Hand, is the most notable surviving Gangrel antitribu from the Sabbat's founding generation; most others have succumbed to the clan's bestial curse and retired to the wilderness or torpor. The influx of experienced Camarilla-defector Gangrel — ancillae unwilling to grind through years of hazing for an Acceptance Rite — has put real strain on established pack hierarchies, forcing pack priests and ducti to actively manage the newcomers as a valuable but volatile resource.

Among the anarchs, Gangrel most often show up as members of nomadic biker gangs rather than city-based Anarch Free State politics; most anarch Gangrel are running from something rather than organizing toward anything. A notable named anarch faction is the Valkyries, an all-female Gangrel group led by Brunhilde, based in Scandinavia and radiating influence into the European anarch movement; a splinter group of four Valkyries has relocated to the West Coast Anarch Free State (California) to investigate a wave of targeted attacks on bestial-featured Gangrel anarchs by Asian vampires (Cathayans) moving up the coast from Chinatowns.

Most Gangrel, antitribu included, follow the Path (Road) of Humanity; those who erode past it most often adopt the Path of the Feral Heart (already documented separately in this system). Clanbook: Gangrel notes the clan's relative representation on the other Paths of Enlightenment, useful for Storytellers placing NPCs or advising players building elder/ancilla Gangrel who have left Humanity:

  • Path of Caine: rare among Gangrel, but the few who qualify (intelligent, tenacious Noddist researchers) stand out.
  • Path of Cathari: a fair number of both City and Country Gangrel are found here — the Beast Within wallowing in excess rather than mud.
  • Path of Death and the Soul: holds almost no interest for Gangrel; its dispassionate outlook runs against the clan's temperament.
  • Path of Evil Revelations: very few Gangrel are drawn to infernalism, but the rare exceptions worry the Sabbat's Inquisitors precisely because they roam Sabbat and Camarilla territory alike with equal disregard.
  • Path of Honorable Accord: few in number, but highly respected by other Gangrel for its straightforward code.
  • Path of Lilith: attractive to Gangrel chasing the clan's apocryphal connection to Lilith (through Ennoia); Gangrel generally leave Bahari followers alone even if they don't join them.
  • Path of Power and the Inner Voice: extremely rare successes are formidable; many ambitious young Gangrel attempt it and fail, undone by their own Beasts.

The Ahrimanes were a secretive bloodline created during the Sabbat's early expansion into the Americas by a Gangrel antitribu named Muricia, who performed a ritual that separated her from the rest of Clan Gangrel, permanently destroying her ability to sire progeny or form blood bonds, in exchange for an innate connection to the spirit world. Every subsequent Ahrimane has been created from a female Gangrel (usually Native American, with African-American women the next largest group), through a process only Muricia is known to be able to perform. The entire bloodline vanished without explanation in early 1998; their havens sit empty and the Sabbat has no confirmed answer, though some blame a second Tremere purge of thaumaturges.

Disciplines: Animalism, Auspex, Protean, plus a bloodline-unique variant of Thaumaturgy invoking the spirits of the natural world (built from Lure of Flames, Movement of the Mind, Elemental Mastery, the Green Path, Neptune's Might, Spirit Manipulation, and Weather Control).

Weakness: As with all artificially-thinned blood, an Ahrimane may not sire childer or blood bond vampires or mortals (she may still create ghouls, and may still be bound by others). Because every Ahrimane was once a Gangrel, most retain a handful of animalistic features from before they left the clan.

pages.name: Gangrel Bloodlines: City Gangrel and Mariners

text.content:
City Gangrel descend from the first Sabbat Gangrel packs founded in the New World, tracing back to a ritual performed by seven founding packs whose participants have never confirmed what actually happened that night. City Gangrel are almost exclusively Sabbat; the few independents or Autarkis among them are typically Camarilla defectors, and a City Gangrel who joins the Camarilla outright earns a spot on the Sabbat's Wild Hunt target list. Disciplines: Celerity, Obfuscate, Protean (in place of the parent clan's Animalism and Fortitude). They share the standard Gangrel weakness (accumulating animal features from frenzy). Favored Paths of Enlightenment mirror the main clan's Feral Heart, with a minority on Lilith or Power and the Inner Voice.

Mariners (called "Gangrel aquarii" derisively by the Tremere) are Gangrel who have taken to the sea, using variant Protean powers (sonar, razor-sharp webbing) that any Gangrel may learn regardless of bloodline. What sets Mariners apart as a bloodline is a more severe version of the clan curse: Mariners lose a Social Attribute for every three animal features acquired, rather than every five, due to their unusually fast acquisition of extreme aquatic/insectoid features (scales, tentacles, fins, squid beaks). The Mariners have been offered membership in both the Camarilla and the Sabbat and have declined both, as individuals, every time; their reaction to the Gangrel leaving the Camarilla has been indifference. At Storyteller discretion, since insectoid/ichthyoid features have grown more common clan-wide in the modern nights, the Mariners' harsher 1-per-3 threshold may be relaxed back to the standard 1-per-5 to reflect that the rest of the clan has caught up in strangeness.

pages.name: Gangrel Extinct/Uncertain Bloodlines: Anda, Laibon, Lhiannan

text.content:
Clanbook: Gangrel identifies several bloodlines of suspected (not confirmed) Gangrel origin, useful as Storyteller-controlled NPC lineages or chronicle hooks rather than open character options:

  • Anda ("blood brother" in Mongolian): steppe-nomad Gangrel who rode with the Mongol hordes, using Fortitude, Protean, and a unique nomad-suited variant of Animalism. Wiped out to the last vampire by the vampires of China at the close of the Yuan Dynasty; any survivors have been in torpor for seven centuries or more with no sign of waking.
  • Laibon: a reclusive African bloodline of uncertain Gangrel descent, sharing Animalism and Fortitude with the parent clan. Their unique Abombwe Discipline is theorized to involve a pact with the Beast Within (tithing vitae to it) that spares them the slow personality erosion that plagues Gangrel. Now numbering fewer than a dozen individuals who maintain any contact with wider vampire society.
  • Lhiannan: a pagan Western European bloodline eradicated by the Inquisition by the 14th century, in part due to the political convenience this served the Ventrue, Toreador, and Lasombra of the era. The past 50 years have seen a "neo-Lhiannan" cultural revival (not a true restoration of the bloodline or its lost mystic powers) among Gangrel in Ireland, Scotland, and Wales, linked to descendants of Irish Revolt (1916) Embraces.

pages.name: The Beast Rampant: Animal Features and Mixed Blessings (MET)

text.content:
Every Gangrel frenzy — whether entered willingly, fiercely resisted, or triggered by Rotschreck — leaves a physical or behavioral mark of the Beast, except a Gangrel who successfully obeys the "flight" imperative of Rotschreck. A cornered Gangrel who instead fights during Rotschreck still acquires a new feature. Features are usually visible (fur, feathers, scales, altered facial structure, extra appendages, nictating membranes, etc.) but may instead be behavioral quirks (circling before sitting, marking territory with blood, toying with prey) that function like minor, roleplay-only derangements; the player may spend a Willpower Trait to suppress an animal-behavior quirk for a scene. The Storyteller has final approval over any feature awarded, especially drastic mutations.

Core mechanic: every five animal features (physical or behavioral) accumulated permanently reduces one Social Attribute/Trait by one — usually Appearance first, though Charisma or Manipulation may be affected instead by the Storyteller's discretion (mental/behavioral features more often hit Charisma or Manipulation). Lost Social Traits may later be bought back with experience, roleplayed as the character compensating (concealing clothing, voice/charm training, etc.); the buy-back cost is calculated from the character's original (pre-frenzy) Trait value, and generation-based Attribute caps apply to that original value, not the reduced one.

Mixed Blessings (rare, drastic mutations): the Storyteller may award one of the following in extreme circumstances (a botch, or a long and bloody frenzy); a Gangrel should generally only ever acquire one. Each provides a mechanical benefit alongside its social cost, and each can be concealed with effort but inflicts a Trait penalty on Social tests if left exposed (roughly a two-Trait penalty per the main clan write-up unless noted).

  • Frog Eyes: two-Trait bonus on sight-based Perception tests; one fewer Trait penalty than normal for facing multiple opponents.
  • Exoskeleton: two bonus Physical Traits for Strength-related tests, plus one extra level of armor vs. bashing/lethal damage; however, anyone trying to stake the vampire only needs to win or tie a single Simple Test after winning the Physical Challenge (instead of the usual three).
  • Hide/Carapace: two levels of armor vs. bashing and lethal damage, one level vs. aggravated damage; one-Trait penalty on Dexterity-related tests.
  • Maw: bite inflicts two levels of aggravated damage and drains three Blood Traits per turn while feeding; cannot be hidden by closing the mouth.
  • Sonar: two-Trait bonus navigating in darkness, fog, or smoke; a character with the Medicine Ability may notice the voice alteration with a Mental Challenge. Ears cannot be concealed while in use.
  • Spinnerets: spend one Blood Trait to generate a square yard of webbing or 10 feet of a single strand; breaking it requires winning a Static Physical Challenge against the Gangrel's Physical Trait total (one-Trait bonus to the breaker if using claws/a blade). Observers may notice the spinnerets with a Mental Challenge; the Gangrel takes a two-Trait penalty resisting that notice. Sunlight or bright artificial light destroys the webbing within 10 turns.
  • Tail: inflicts two levels of bashing damage as a natural weapon; observers need a Mental Challenge (three-Trait penalty to the Gangrel) to notice it if concealed.
  • Talons: function as Wolf Claws on both hands and feet but cannot retract; one-Trait penalty on fine manipulation tasks.
  • Venom: a successful bite forces the target into a Static Physical Test against eight Traits or lose one Physical Trait (heals as aggravated damage; the victim falls unconscious at two Physical Traits remaining). Any failed bite attack requires two Simple Tests; failing both breaks one or both fangs, which regrow on the aggravated-damage healing schedule.
  • Wings: two-Trait bonus on balance-related tests; falling damage is one level of bashing per 15 feet instead of per 10.

pages.name: Gangrel Discipline Powers (Advanced Animalism, Fortitude, Protean) - MET

text.content:
Clanbook: Gangrel presents several higher-level Discipline powers, developed by the clan's elders, with native MET conversions. These are new to this sourcebook and are not duplicates of the already-catalogued Quell the Beast, Subsume the Spirit, or Drawing Out the Beast entries in packs/disciplines/.

Animalism

Stampede (Level Seven): triggers mass panic-flight in an already-agitated crowd of roughly 50+ mortals. Make a Static Social Challenge against a Trait total equal to the highest Willpower in the crowd; the Stampede affects everyone within 50 yards, extendable another 50 yards per additional Social Trait spent. Targets at or below half the Gangrel's Social Trait total succumb automatically; targets at or above half may spend a Willpower Trait to resist with a Static Social Challenge against the Gangrel's total; targets whose Willpower equals or exceeds the Gangrel's Social Trait total may make the same resistance test without spending Willpower.

Crimson Fury (Level Eight): a permanent, always-on power. Anyone feeding on the Gangrel must win a Self-Control Test against four Traits or enter frenzy immediately. Anyone attempting to diablerize the Gangrel must spend one Willpower point per turn of the attempt. A successful diablerist suffers a permanent one-Trait penalty on all future frenzy checks (and falls into Wassail at Self-Control 1 instead of 0), plus a recurring Willpower Test contest against the consumed Gangrel's Beast (weekly for year one, monthly for year two, yearly thereafter) — the loser of each contest permanently loses a Willpower Trait.

Eyes of the Forest (Level Nine): the Gangrel spreads her awareness through a defined geographic domain (a valley, mountain, wood), seeing/hearing through its animals and insects and gaining safety from direct attack while interred; significant damage to the domain (fire, strip mining, chemical contamination) instead damages the vampire and may force her out. If two Animalism masters claim the same domain, the one with greater Willpower prevails.

Fortitude

Sensory Shield (Level Six): spend two Blood Traits; for one hour, the vampire is immune to overwhelming mundane sensory input (searchlights, gunfire, pepper spray) even while using powers like Heightened Senses, and takes two fewer Traits of wound penalty (full penalty applies once Sensory Shield ends). A Static Fortitude-level Test can reduce Trait penalties from severe environmental hazards. Glowing wounds/orifices impose a two-Trait penalty on Social Challenges against mortals while active.

Resilient Mind (Level Seven): on learning this power, make an Extended Static Willpower Test against eight Traits; each success discards one derangement or two animal-behavior flaws (lost Social Traits from those flaws remain lost). Grants a permanent three-Trait bonus resisting mind-altering Disciplines/magic (not Presence or other emotion-affecting powers). If a new derangement is later imposed, a Static Willpower Test against seven Traits (spending three Mental Traits on success, no Willpower spend for retests) lets it fade after one night and the following day instead of persisting.

King of the Mountain (Level Eight): spend three Blood Traits to activate for one hour. The vampire uses full Trait totals on all defensive actions (offense still splits the pool as normal). Attackers must win an initial Physical Challenge (ties favor the defender); if the attacker fails, their weapon shatters (unless enchanted) and they take the damage instead; if they tie, the weapon shatters but they take no damage; if they win, they must still win a Simple Test to actually land damage (Superior Potence skips this last test).

Protean

Shape of the Beast Revisited (Level Four, Gangrel-only variant): the Gangrel defines a "fight" form and a "flight" form when learning this power (fixed thereafter, unlike the standard wolf/bat-only version other clans use). Spend a Blood Trait to transform (three turns, reducible to one by spending up to three Blood Traits); lasts until dawn or until voluntarily ended. Each form adds five bonus Traits split across at least two of Strength/Dexterity/Stamina/Perception/Wits-related categories (fixed once chosen). Bite inflicts two levels and claws one level of aggravated damage by default (Storyteller may reweight for the animal in question). Movement doubles in animal form. The flight form is capped at three Physical Traits (from the character's normal list), flies at running speed, and permits declaring Fair Escape once five paces from the nearest non-superior-speed pursuer; attacks against it take a two-Trait penalty unless the character opts to keep full Strength-related Traits instead.

Shape Mastery (Level Six): forces another shapeshifter back into their base form. Requires getting a Blood Trait's worth of the Gangrel's vitae onto the target (a successful Physical Challenge to smear it on by force, or a Mental Challenge to apply it covertly), then spending a second Blood Trait and winning a Social Challenge; on success the target must stay in human/base form for one hour or until the blood is fully removed. Works against Obtenebration, Protean, Serpentis, Thaumaturgy, and Vicissitude shapeshifting (levels six and below) and against Lupine/werecreature natural shapeshifting.

Animal Swarm (Level Seven): the vampire disperses into one small creature per current Blood Trait (or fewer, larger creatures sharing Blood Traits evenly). Lasts until sunrise or voluntary reformation; any creatures not reabsorbed by dawn are destroyed. Difficult to represent at the table — Storytellers should plan in advance how a single player represents a swarm.

Mythic Form (Level Eight): spend three Blood Traits (transformation takes three turns, cannot be hastened, but the character may act normally during it) to become a culturally-rooted mythic beast (griffin, thunderbird, sphinx, dragon, etc. — characters from cultures without a mythic-beast tradition cannot use this power). Grants nine bonus Traits (at least one each to Strength/Dexterity/Stamina-related categories, remainder flexible), two extra Bruised and two extra Hurt health levels, the effects of Heightened Senses, Eyes of the Beast, and Awe, three levels of aggravated close-combat damage divided among natural weapons, and one ranged attack per turn (Physical Challenge; two levels of aggravated damage per Blood Trait spent, range and area scaled to Physical Trait total). Sample form (Dragon) given in the source: flight, three levels of armor, one-level bite and claw, fiery-breath ranged attack.

Combination Disciplines

Claw Immunity (Animalism 2, Fortitude 4): spend two Blood Traits and name an animal type; doubles the effect of Fortitude when soaking that animal's natural bite/claw damage for the next hour (18 XP to learn per the print cost, informational only).

Flesh Wound (Fortitude 2, Obfuscate 3): spend one Blood Trait; for one hour, no damage the vampire suffers produces any visible sign (no wounds, limping, or bleeding) until the power ends, though existing damage still applies mechanically. Auspex users may pierce it with the standard Auspex-vs-Obfuscate challenge; bystanders may attempt a Mental Challenge if the lack of injury becomes implausible. Grants a two-Trait bonus on Social Tests about the character's physical state while active.

See the Reflected Form (Auspex 4, Protean 4): a Mental Challenge reveals a target's Protean beast forms or their single most powerful shapeshifting form from another Discipline; an additional Mental Trait reveals all defined forms; a further Mental Trait reveals potential forms and the emotions tied to the target's shapeshifting. Does not detect Mask of a Thousand Faces (not a true shapechange).

Beast Meld (Animalism 3, Protean 6): spend three Blood Traits and win a Physical Challenge to merge with an animal host at least as large as the vampire's smallest beast form. One Mental Trait gives the animal general directions, two gives specific commands; the vampire must set a release condition in advance. The vampire takes no damage suffered by the host except fire damage (soakable with Fortitude); if the host is killed by violence, the vampire is immediately expelled.
